newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close slightly up on late buying. [CORRECTED 11:06 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close slightly up on late buying. [CORRECTED 11:06 GMT]

text.p: Late active buying in some secondaries helped Jakarta share prices close slightly up on Friday after coming under pressure from profit-taking during the afternoon session, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 0.44 points, or 0.07 percent, to close at 657.87 points after touching a low of 656.08 points. Gainers led losers by 60 to 45, with 68 counters unchanged.
The index closed up 11.38 points (corrects from 20.44 points), 2.0 percent (corrects from 3.0 percent), on the week.
Brokers said the market was likely to be mixed on Monday with overseas buyers expected to concentrate on a few big-capitalised stocks.
But possible profit-taking could keep the index within a narrow range, they said.
Brokers said mixed regional markets, including sharp falls in Tokyo, had helped dampen sentiment.
"But overall the correction in Jakarta is more due to technical aspects," an analyst with a Singapore-firm said.
Strong buying interest in some secondaries including newly-listed companies such as Alter Abadi, Bank Pikko and Bank Umum Servitia had helped the index inch up, brokers said.
Kaolin miner Alter Abadi rose 125 rupiah to 1,150 and topped the active list with 13.2 million shares changing hands. Brokers said it was active after its encouraging debut on Thursday.
Bank Pikko was also rose on active locally-led buying, rising 50 rupiah to 950 on 10.4 million shares, brokers said.
Bank Umum Servitia, which listed last December, rose 25 rupiah to 1,025 on 1.8 million shares on fresh buying due to perceptions that its price was relatively low, brokers said.
Heavyweight Telkom was actively traded, rising 25 rupiah to 4,200 on 2.5 million shares.
But some banking stocks and heavyweights including Bank BDNI, Bank International Indonesia and Semen Gresik were pressured on profit-taking, brokers said.
Semen Gresik fell 300 rupiah to 7,300 on 1.5 million shares on profit-taking after recent rises, they said.
Bank International Indonesia fell 75 rupiah to 1,775 on 4.5 million shares, while Bank BDNI fell 25 rupiah to 2,375 on 2.7 million shares.
